note: The decision procedure: an ORDERED list of rules over the typed facts. The first rule whose `when` clause is satisfied decides the verdict and the code; if none is, the verdict is the default. This is what makes the pack an ORACLE rather than a list of assertions -- before it existed, `expected` and `refusal_code` were free author input and nothing checked them against the scenario's own facts. `bin/pack-check` now DERIVES every row's verdict from its facts and refuses the row if the derivation disagrees.
how_to_read: Each rule names the pinned policy it enforces (source/parameters.json), the fact values that trigger it, the verdict it produces and the denial code (source/denial_codes.json). The ORDER is the evaluation order and is itself part of the pinned policy: a revoked approval is reported as revoked even though it is also unconsumed, and an expired approval is reported as expired even though it may also lack a second seat.
order_note: Ordered most-specific defect first. Two orderings matter and are deliberate: expiry is evaluated BEFORE seat count, so T1-F5-coapprove-after-expiry-001 reports the expiry that PREVENTED the second seat rather than the missing seat it caused; and revocation is evaluated BEFORE consumption, so T1-F7-replay-after-revoke-001 reports the revocation rather than the replay.

rules.note: AC-05_ODP clause 1. No shipped row triggers it; it exists so the rule set is closed over the pinned policies rather than over the defects that happened to be interesting.

No pinned rule speaks to execution rate -- see source/parameters.json `unpinned_by_design`. The verdict is `unresolvable` BECAUSE the dimension feeds nothing, which is why `execution_burst` deliberately declares `feeds: []`.

default.note: Every pinned policy is satisfied. This is the sufficiency rule the first v2 review found missing: an `allow` is derivable only because the core dimensions are ALL stated and none of them triggers a rule. `trace_encoding` triggers nothing, which is precisely why the four harness rows are `allow` -- their defect is in the comparator's encoding, not in the authorization.
